key_insight: The paper shows that distributed quantum circuit knitting can be made classically tractable by exploiting a weak-coupling partition, reducing reconstruction cost from exponential to polynomial.
engineering_relevance: This enables more scalable approximate quantum computing workflows by letting larger circuits be executed across distributed resources with controlled classical overhead.
method: Partition the circuit around a weakly coupled qubit
Approximate the distributed process so classical reconstruction scales polynomially
Demonstrate the approach on layered circuits inspired by QAOA
evidence_signal: The abstract claims the method reduces the classical cost from exponential to polynomial and validates it on a layered QAOA-style circuit.
watch_item: The approach relies on a weak-coupling assumption, so accuracy and scalability may degrade when the partitioned qubits are strongly entangled.
paper_title: Scalable quantum circuit knitting using a weak-coupling approximation
